title: Opening Past-Due Release of Disability Compensation: Months Owed and Amount Standing Paid
content:
**Formal clause.** The opening past-due release on a Disability Compensation award is the compensation owed for the months owed, less what stands paid against it, and never less than nothing; it is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Months owed.** The months owed are the whole months elapsed from the award's effective date to the issue date of the most recent monthly payment on the award.

**Compensation owed.** The compensation owed is the veteran-alone rate of the award's combined rating for each month owed, as the Disability Compensation rate table gives it for the tier the award carries.

**What stands paid.** What stands paid against the opening past-due release is the gross of every monthly payment issued, less the gross of every payment that came back, plus the gross of every replacement and of every past-due release already on the award.

**Worked figure (hypothetical award at Disability Compensation (60% Combined Rating)).**

1. Award effective date: 15 September 2025. Most recent monthly payment issued: 1 April 2026. Whole months elapsed: 6.
2. Compensation owed: 1435.02 multiplied by 6, that is 8610.12.
3. Monthly payments issued: one, for March, gross 1435.02; nothing came back; no replacement or earlier release. What stands paid: 1435.02.
4. Opening past-due release: 8610.12 less 1435.02, that is 7175.10.

**Floor.** If what stands paid were 9000.00 against compensation owed of 8610.12, the release would be nothing, never a negative amount.
